ai.description: *Ahaetulla dispar* is a slender, 1-meter-long snake. It features a bright green dorsum, a yellow ventrolateral stripe, and a distinctively pointed, elongated snout. It belongs to the family Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla dispar* is best distinguished by its distinctively short, blunt snout and a lack of a pointed rostral appendage, unlike the elongated snouts of other vine snakes.
ai.habitat: Ahaetulla dispar inhabits the high-altitude montane cloud forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Ahaetulla dispar is primarily diurnal, actively hunting small lizards and frogs by using its keen binocular vision and slender, camouflaged body to strike with precision.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla dispar* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. It typically produces a small litter of 2–6 offspring, with breeding occurring during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla dispar* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
